title: Revoking a Federated Identity cuts the workload off
lede: A workload presents the token its platform issued. The gateway verifies it on every request and reads the identity's state. After the operator revokes the identity the token is still valid, but the next request is refused. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Simulated.

nodes.label: Backend with the app's own credential

edges.label: allowed: app's credential, token not forwarded

steps.title: The platform issues a token
steps.what: A Kubernetes service account or a CI job gets a short-lived token from its own platform. Nothing long-lived is stored in the workload.

steps.title: The workload calls the gateway
steps.what: Every request carries the platform token. The same identity can reach MCP servers, peer agents and LLM providers; scopes tell them apart.

steps.title: The gateway checks the signature
steps.what: It verifies the token against the issuer's key set. The set is cached and refreshed every 15 minutes (the deck); during an outage the last known good set is used.

steps.title: The gateway checks the identity
steps.what: Issuer, subject and audience must match a registered Federated Identity exactly, and the identity must be active. This state is read on every request.

steps.title: Allowed: the backend gets its own credential
steps.what: The token stops at the gateway. The backend receives the application's own configured credential, never the workload's token.

steps.title: Every decision is recorded
steps.what: Each request is written to the audit trail with the identity and the deployment (subject) it came from.

steps.title: The operator revokes the identity
steps.what: One action on the identity. Nothing is sent to the workload or to the platform.

steps.title: The gateway reads the new state
steps.what: On the next request the registry says revoked. This is how the lab reads the deck's word immediately; the deck gives no number.

steps.title: The next request is refused
steps.what: The token is still valid (signature, binding, lifetime), but the identity is not, so the answer is 403. The refusal is attributed to the same deployment.
